description: This Java source file defines a utility class 'NaturalStrings' that provides methods for natural string comparison operations, including locale-aware and ASCII-based comparators, with features such as numeric ordering within strings.

classes.name: NaturalStrings
classes.description: Utility class for natural String comparison operations, providing various comparators and comparison methods.

methods.name: getNaturalComparator
methods.description: Returns a comparator that compares contained numbers based on their numeric values and compares other parts using the current locale's order rules.

methods.name: getNaturalComparator(final Collator collator)
methods.description: Returns a comparator that compares contained numbers based on their numeric values and compares other parts using the given collator.

methods.name: getNaturalComparatorAscii
methods.description: Returns a comparator that compares contained numbers based on their numeric values and compares other parts based on each character's Unicode value (ASCII).

methods.name: getNaturalComparatorIgnoreCaseAscii
methods.description: Returns a comparator that compares contained numbers based on their numeric values and compares other parts ignoring case differences, based on Unicode values (ASCII).

methods.name: compareNatural
methods.description: Compares two strings using the current locale's rules and comparing contained numbers based on their numeric values.

methods.name: compareNatural(Collator collator, String s, String t)
methods.description: Compares two strings using the given collator and comparing contained numbers based on their numeric values.

methods.name: compareNaturalAscii
methods.description: Compares two strings using character Unicode values for non-digit characters and numeric values for contained numbers, assuming ASCII.

methods.name: compareNaturalIgnoreCaseAscii
methods.description: Compares two strings ignoring case differences and using Unicode values for non-digit characters and numeric values for contained numbers, assuming ASCII.
